  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION

  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH DGREE EXAMINATIONS NOVEMBER 2025  
  Social Networks [CSE_4204]  
  Marks: 50                                                                             Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Evaluate how variations in the structure and type of connections within a network  
  influence its overall behavior, stability, and connectivity patterns. Assess the impact  
  of factors such as density, clustering, and degree distribution on information flow and (5)  
  A)      resilience, and propose strategies to enhance network efficiency or robustness based on  
  the principles of network science.  
  
  B)      Apply the process of network data collection from real-world sources such as social  
  media or biological databases, and interpret how the quality and format of the collected    (3)  
  data influence the reliability of subsequent network modeling.  
  
  C)      Apply your understanding of network analysis tools such as SNAP and Gephi to  
  illustrate how software-based visualization enhances the comprehension of large-scale (2)  
  network structures.  
  
  2)           Evaluate how the balance between strong and weak ties affects the stability,  
  cohesion, and adaptability of a social system. Assess potential risks of over-reliance on  
  either relationship type and propose strategies for maintaining an optimal mix of ties to (5)  
  A)      promote robust social connectivity.  
  
  B)      Identify an approach to measure homophily in a real-world social network using  
  attributes such as age, profession, or location, and interpret what high or low             (3)  
  homophily values indicate about the diversity of the network.  
  
  C)      Construct a simple triadic relationship among three individuals to illustrate how balance  
  or conflict can emerge within a social structure.                                         (2)  
  
  3)           Compare and contrast the results obtained from degree and eigenvector centrality  
  when analyzing a social or communication network. Assess how each measure captures  
  (5)  
  a different aspect of node importance and network hierarchy.  
  A)  
  B)      Apply the PageRank algorithm to develop a simple example network and interpret  
  how node ranking changes with variations in link structure, demonstrating its role in       (3)  
  information retrieval and web search optimization.  
  
  C)      Construct a simple example to illustrate how the threshold model determines whether         (2)  
  a user adopts a new idea based on the number of influenced neighbors.

  4)                Evaluate the significance of power-law distributions in understanding real-world  
  networks such as the web, citation networks, or social media. Assess how the presence  
  of a few highly connected nodes influences network stability, vulnerability, and         (5)  
  A)           information flow.  
  
  B)           Apply the SI, SIS, and SIR epidemic models to illustrate how disease or information  
  spreads over time within a network, and interpret how recovery and reinfection rates     (3)  
  influence the overall diffusion process.  
  
  C)           Apply the concept of a scale-free network to identify how a few highly connected  
  nodes (hubs) influence the structure and connectivity of the network.                    (2)  
  
  5)                Compare the Watts-Strogatz small-world model with a random network model to  
  evaluate how features such as short average path lengths and high clustering  
  (5)  
  coefficients explain the balance between randomness and structure in real networks.  
  A)  
  B)           Develop an example of viral content propagation in an online social platform to  
  interpret how network structure and peer influence contribute to the speed and reach     (3)  
  of virality.  
  
  C)           Illustrate, with a brief example, how digital marketing campaigns make use of  
  network influence to enhance the virality of promotional content.                        (2)
